title: Stability Ops Accelerator and Operator Runloop
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview
========
This document defines the Stability Ops Accelerator: a compact, operator-focused incident process and runloop optimized for model-serving platforms. It consolidates the incident lifecycle, operator runbooks, rotation scheduling rules, game-day scenarios, status page automation patterns, and customer comm templates into a single, prescriptive reference intended for SREs, service owners, and response engineers.

Scope
-----
- Applies to Redwood inference production services (hosted, dedicated, private control plane).
- Covers incidents that affect latency, throughput, correctness (model quality), and availability of inference endpoints.
- Excludes: deployment planning, long-term roadmap decisions, and non-production labs.

Quick summary (one-line)
------------------------
When an SLO or customer-impacting signal trips, follow the 3-stage runloop: Acknowledge -> Contain -> Restore; escalate using the Ordered Escalation Ladder; use templates to drive customer comms and capture evidence for the postmortem quality gate.

Roles and responsibilities
--------------------------
- Operator (primary responder): owns initial acknowledgement, triage, and executing containment runbook steps.
- Bridge lead (senior SRE): orchestrates cross-team coordination, external comms, and decisions about rollbacks/fallbacks.
- Service owner (team lead): approves high-impact changes, provides product context and customer impact assessment.
- On-call escalation tier (tier-2/3): provides specialist remediation (runtime kernels, model variants, infra).
- Incident comms owner (customer success / bridge lead): drafts status page and customer messages.

Incident lifecycle (detailed steps)
----------------------------------
1) Alert & acknowledge (T+0 to T+5)
   - Pager triggers; operator acknowledges within 5 minutes.
   - Record the alert ID and initial hypothesis in the incident channel.
2) Initial triage (T+0 to T+15)
   - Confirm customer impact using metrics: requests/sec, 95/99 latency, error rate, tokens/sec, KV-cache hit rate.
   - Classify severity (SEV1/SEV2/SEV3) using definition table below.
3) Containment (T+15 to T+60)
   - Apply immediate mitigations from containment runbooks (scale up, fallback to cheaper model, activate read-only caches, rate-limit or burst-throttle ingress).
   - If multi-region, failover policy executes per the routing playbook.
4) Restoration (T+1h onward)
   - Implement targeted fixes (kernel/driver restart, cache purge+warm, model rollback, config patch).
   - Run smoke tests on a controlled traffic slice; slowly ramp traffic back using canary policy.
5) Stabilize & close (post-restoration)
   - Confirm SLOs are restored for a minimum observation window (30–60 minutes).
   - Collect evidence, save logs, and open a postmortem.

Severity classification (reference)
----------------------------------
| SEV | Symptom examples | Customer impact threshold | Immediate action |
|-----|------------------|--------------------------|------------------|
| SEV1 | Total outage for >3% of active tenants in a region | Customer API returns 5xx or no responses | Bridge, exec-notify, global failover |
| SEV2 | Latency spike >2x baseline for 10+ minutes for high QPS endpoints | Significant degradation for key customers | Containment runbooks, regional failover |
| SEV3 | Single-tenant QoS regression or degraded quality for low traffic | Isolated impact, elevated errors | Owner triage, scheduled fix window |

Runbook catalog (core entries)
-----------------------------
- model-serving-degradation: latency and cold-KV-cache runbook
  - Symptoms: 95th latency increasing, KV-cache hit rate < 70%, CPU on worker nodes > 90%
  - Immediate steps: switch to reduced-length generation model variant; enable prefix caching; increase batch timeout to 25ms
  - Escalation: owner -> runtime-kernels -> infra-networking

- kernel-crash-and-oom: node-level fatal errors and OOMs
  - Symptoms: pod restarts, CUDA OOM logs, kernel-level crashes in /var/log
  - Immediate steps: cordon node, restart runtime on new worker, purge large KV entries, set eviction policy to LRU-fast

- ttl-cache-poisoning: corrupted prefix or evicted warm cache causing repeated slow-paths
  - Steps: rotate cache namespace, run controlled rewarm script, throttle traffic to rewarm target nodes

Example runbook table (condensed)
--------------------------------
- Name: model-serving-degradation
  Owner: eng-serving-runtime
  Pager: #oncall-ml-serving
  Primary mitigation: model-variant-fallback, KV-cache-rewarm
  Time-to-contain target: 30 min

Rotation scheduling and fairness rules
------------------------------------
- Primary constraint: no engineer should have more than one critical pager shift within a 7-day window.
- Shift length: 8-hour blocks for primary operators; 24-hour for tiered on-call (overlap handoff at 08:00 UTC).
- Swap rules: allow one self-swap per 30-day period; swaps must be recorded in the oncall roster and approved by rotation owner.
- Auto-scheduling algorithm (summary): round-robin across on-call pool with weighted fairness (weights by recent load: recent-shifts*1.2). This yields ~10% bias to less-burned responders to maintain knowledge spread.

Game days: scenarios and rubrics
--------------------------------
Purpose: validate operator runloop, cross-team handoffs, and containment runbooks. Rundays are quarterly.

Core scenarios (rotate each quarter):
- KV cache warm-loss: synthetic traffic removes cache entries and forces cold paths (focus: cache rewarm, traffic shaping).
- Multi-model-fallback stress: primary model overloaded, require fallback and correctness checks (focus: A/B routing, quality regression detection).
- Throttle storm / noisy neighbor: noisy tenant consumes capacity, triggers autoscaler and backpressure (focus: admission control, tenant isolation).

Grading rubric (pass/fail metrics):
- Acknowledge within 5m: 10 points
- Contain within SLA targets (see runbook): 40 points
- Customer comm posted within 15m if SEV1/2: 20 points
- Evidence capture complete and postmortem opened within 4h: 20 points
- Coordination and handoff quality (subjective): 10 points
Pass threshold: >=75 points.

Status page automation patterns
------------------------------
We maintain an automated status pipeline to reduce noise and speed transparent comms. The recommended pattern:
1) Use an internal incident registry (inc-registry service) to create incident records.
2) A small automation lambda (node/python) composes status page messages and pushes to the public status page API and to the incident channel.
3) Templates are chosen by severity and updated by the comms owner.

Minimal example (curl) to update status API:
curl -X POST https://status.redwood.ai/api/v1/incidents \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $STATUS_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"title":"Model serving latency spike - us-west1","impact":"partial_outage","updates":[{"body":"We are investigating elevated latencies for text generation endpoints in us-west1. Operators are containing traffic and activating fallback models.","status":"investigating"}] }'

Customer communication templates (copy-and-send)
-----------------------------------------------
- Initial SEV1 notice (public):
We are currently investigating elevated latencies and failed responses for text generation endpoints in the us-west1 region. Our engineers are actively containing the issue by routing traffic to healthy model variants and rewarming caches. We will provide updates every 15 minutes or sooner as significant milestones occur.

- Customer-visibility update (15m):
Update: We have put a mitigation in place that reduces error rates by ~65% and latency by ~30% for affected calls. Work continues on a full restoration; we estimate a further 45–90 minutes to complete verification and traffic ramp.

- Post-incident customer summary (post-closure):
Summary: On YYYY-MM-DD at HH:MM UTC we detected elevated latencies for hosted generation endpoints in us-west1 impacting ~X% of requests. Root cause: cache eviction cascade combined with model variant overload. Mitigation: triggered fallback to smaller model variant and rewarm pipeline; system restored by HH:MM UTC. Action items: (1) increase default cache retention for hot prefixes, (2) add model-variant warm replicas, (3) alert thresholds to include KV-cache-hit-rate.

Postmortem template and quality gate
------------------------------------
Use the postmortem template integrated with the postmortem tracker. Minimum required fields:
- Title, incident ID, SEV, start/end timestamps
- Chronology (timeline of key events, 5–10min granularity for first hour)
- Impact statement (customers affected, business impact)
- Root cause analysis (one-paragraph hypothesis, evidence, instrumentation links)
- Mitigations and timeline (what changed during incident)
- Long-term action items with owner and ETA (must include at least one owner with target completion < 90 days)
- Postmortem quality gate checklist (signed off by Bridge lead and service owner):
  - Evidence attached (logs, graphs)
  - Correlating alerts and traces present
  - Customer comms thread linked
  - Action items assigned and visible in tracker

Runbook maintenance and ownership
--------------------------------
- Owners must review their runbooks quarterly and after any SEV1/SEV2 incident.
- Deprecated runbooks are archived with a migration note.
- Runbook change log must include: date, author, summary of change, reviewer.

Appendix: operator cheat-sheet (condensed)
-----------------------------------------
- First 5 minutes: acknowledge, open incident channel, post initial comm, capture hypothesis.
- First 30 minutes: contain using the runbook, apply mitigations, escalate if blocked.
- After restore: gather evidence, open postmortem, schedule action item review with service owner within 3 business days.

Appendix: example Slack messages
-------------------------------
Initial alert channel message:
[INC-12345] SEV1: Elevated latency in us-west1 for text-gen endpoints. Operator @aisha acknowledged. Initial hypothesis: KV cache miss storm; switching to model-variant-v2 for 10% traffic now.

Customer public status snippet (short):
Investigating: Elevated latencies for text-generation in us-west1. We are containing impact and will post updates every 15 minutes.

Maintenance of this document
---------------------------
Owner: eng-serving-runtime documentation lead.
Review cadence: annually and after any major incident.
Feedback: file an update request in the doc comments or ping #runbook-maintainers.
